record_layout.use: namespace type; log 'NSID %d NSType %d NSSize %u' at 0x9c7e8d4 (cc5) / 0x9c7e8f0 (cd8)
logged as NSSize ('%s::%d:NSSize\t\t: %u' 0x8cdcec); ALSO the expected NCAP comparison value in ValidateNamespaceSize (ldr w8,[x9] where x9 = fNamespaces+4+nsid*12: i.e. record[nsid-1].word2)

namespace_struct.word2_note: word2 is the DT-declared size (logged as NSSize) AND the expected-NCAP comparison value in ValidateNamespaceSize (ldr w8,[x9] where x9 = fNamespaces+4+nsid*12; compared against the u32 at Identify buffer+8 = NCAP). For NSID1 (word2=0) the alternate size path uses [x19,#0x4b8] ('Burn-in blks set. NSID1 now sized to %lld') or the caller-supplied capacity (inByteCapacity). Capacity unit is LBAs because NCAP is defined in logical blocks.

word2_semantics.statement: DT NSSize (word2) / expected namespace capacity in LBAs, cross-checked against Identify Namespace NCAP

Apple internal operation selector 0x11 with a 0x1000-byte response buffer whose parsed layout matches Identify Namespace: parses FLBAS (byte 0x1a) and LBAF entry (offset 0x80 + 4*flbas), checks METADATA_SIZE==0, then asserts logicalBlockSize==4096 (0x8cde5b) or logs 'Invalid LogicalBlockSize=%d' (0x8cdde8); compares Identify NCAP (offset 8) against fNamespaces record word2

identify_path.identify_namespace: operation issued via Apple internal selector 0x11 (0x1000-byte buffer) through the command-object wrapper 0xfffffff00ab205ec; the Identify buffer layout (NCAP@8, NLBAF@0x19, FLBAS@0x1a, LBAF@0x80) matches the standard Identify Namespace data structure and is the current-build proof basis

fields.name: NCAP
fields.use: the low u32 at buffer+8 is compared against DT-declared word2 for the NSID (ldr w8,[x0,#8] at 0x9c7ec04)

fields.name: NLBAF
fields.use: num LBA formats; FLBAS must be < NLBAF+1 (b.hs reject at 0x9c7ebe4)

fields.name: LBAF table
fields.use: exact current-build checks: u16 at entry+0 must be ZERO (ldrh + cbnz at 0x9c7ebf4); u8 at entry+2 must equal 12 (cmp w8,#0xc at 0x9c7ebfc); logicalBlockSize = 1<<entry+2 = 4096; on mismatch 'Invalid LogicalBlockSize = %d' with 1<<entry2 and assert '( logicalBlockSize == 4096 )' (0x8cde5b)

identify_path.derivation: LBA size comes from the Identify Namespace LBAF entry selected by FLBAS: entry+0 u16 must be zero and entry+2 u8 is the size exponent; the driver computes logicalBlockSize = 1 << entry+2, logs/asserts it must equal 4096 (exponent 12). It is NOT taken from the DT, not from APFS, and not a standalone hardcoded constant.
identify_path.lba_size_4096_evidence: assert string '( logicalBlockSize == 4096 )' at 0xfffffff0078cde5b used from ValidateNamespaceSize fail path; 'Invalid LogicalBlockSize = %d' 0x8cdde8; LBADS must be 12 (cmp w8,#0xc at 0x9c7ebfc) -> 1<<12 = 4096; range assert 'LBADataSize >= kNVME_512_LBA_Data && LBADataSize <= kNVME_Max_LBA_Data' (0x8d4e0b) with 512_LBA constant string '512' (0x8d2552)
identify_path.offset_8_note: Standard NVMe Identify Namespace layout: NSZE u64 @0x00, NCAP u64 @0x08, NUSE u64 @0x10. The disassembly reads u32 at buffer+8 (ldr w8,[x0,#8] at 0x9c7ec04) with no prior +8 pointer advance, so the compared field is NCAP, not NSZE. Capacity unit remains LBAs either way (NCAP is defined in LBAs).

selector_0x11.evidence: ValidateNamespaceSize passes w0=0x11 to stub 0xfffffff009cd711c (auth-stub slot 0xfffffff0080d0678 -> 0xfffffff00ab205ec command-object wrapper); a sibling path at 0x9c7e650 passes w0=0x12 with a 0x4000 buffer, confirming 0x11/0x12 are an Apple internal operation/selector enum, not the NVMe wire opcode
selector_0x11.wire_opcode: NOT_STATICALLY_RECOVERED - the standard NVMe Admin Identify opcode (0x06) is expected to be written inside the Apple command-object/ANS submission path which is runtime-initialized; claiming the wire opcode would require tracing the command-structure write, which is beyond this gate
selector_0x11.standard_reference: standard NVMe Admin Identify opcode = 0x06 (corroborative reference only)

identify_path.wire_opcode_nonblocking_note: The standard wire opcode byte is NOT required to prove the LBA-size contract: the response layout, LBADS, NCAP, and guest-visible LBA size are all proven from the parsed 0x1000-byte response buffer. Standard Admin Identify opcode 0x06 was NOT observed in Apple runtime code and is recorded only as a corroborative reference.

lba_proof.proof_chain: Identify Namespace -> LBAF[FLBAS].LBADS must equal 12 (cmp w8,#0xc) -> 1<<12 = 4096; failure asserts 'logicalBlockSize == 4096'
lba_proof.capacity_unit: LBA (logical block addresses); NCAP is compared directly against DT word2 without scaling, and NCAP is defined in LBAs; block counts are 'numBlocks' (Identified numBlocks %d Expected numBlocks %d)
lba_proof.overflow_safe: count derived as length/12 via magic-multiply (umull + lsr #35) on u32 length; no shift overflow path found
